2023_10_fy24_proposed_budget_complete_do.paragraph: Oakland Schools' original proposed budget for fiscal year 2023-24, issued March 2023 and circulated to constituent district boards for review and comment as Michigan law requires of intermediate school districts before May 1; it appears in the Troy School District board packet of May 16, 2023. Total proposed funding across all funds is $440.7 million against total proposed expenditures of $455.8 million, with property tax revenue budgeted to grow 5.0%, or $10,962,100, to $230,204,600. The largest single appropriation is the Special Education Fund's PA-18 base distribution to local districts, budgeted at $159,316,800 — up roughly $11.0 million, or 7.4%, from the FY 2022-23 amended budget.

## What it is

Oakland Schools (the Oakland County intermediate school district) original proposed budget for fiscal year 2023-24, dated March 2023 with underlying amendment-report data as of 3/14/2023. It covers all governmental, proprietary and internal service funds, adds five-year operating forecasts for the three major funds, and includes the 5-Year Capital Outlay Plan scheduled for Board first reading on March 21, 2023. ISDs must submit the proposed budget to each constituent district's board by May 1 and adopt by June 30.

## Enterprise-wide totals (FY 2023-24)

| Funding source | Amount | Expenditure category | Amount |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Property taxes | $230.2M | Salary, wage and benefits | $81.5M |
| Other local and investment | $38.3M | Purchased services, supplies, dues/fees | $21.7M |
| State sources | $21.6M | Electric and natural gas utilities | $1.0M |
| Other financing and indirect | $11.7M | Capital outlay | $20.8M |
| Estimated grant awards | $138.9M | Transfers to LEAs and other funds | $188.5M |
| | | Grant-related expenditures | $138.9M |
| | | Payment on existing debt | $3.4M |
| **Total funding** | **$440.7M** | **Total expenditures** | **$455.8M** |

Amounts are net of eligible inter-company eliminated Risk Related Activity Fund revenues and expenses.

## Three major funds

| Fund | FY24 revenue | FY24 expenditures | Result | Ending fund balance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| General Education (100) | $24,344,200 | $24,540,300 | $(196,100) | $6,557,800 (unassigned $4,327,000) |
| Special Education (200) | $183,221,900 | $183,137,500 | $84,400 | $11,524,700 (restricted-SE $1,068,600) |
| Career Focused Education (600) | $49,234,000 | $49,381,200 | $(147,200) | $6,952,400 (restricted $6,912,400) |

Property taxes supply 56% of GEF revenue, 95% of SEF revenue and 86% of CFEF revenue. Fund-level tax budgets rise 5.0%: GEF $13,026,600 to $13,677,900; SEF $165,688,800 to $173,973,200; CFEF $40,527,100 to $42,553,500.

## Key assumptions

- Property taxes +5.0%, a conservative figure against Oakland County Equalization projections of more than 6.0% taxable-value growth; the tax base is 70% principal residence, 30% non-principal residence. No Headlee rollback expected after eight consecutive years of rollbacks.
- Investment revenue budgeted down about 40% district-wide, from $4,911,800 to $2,886,800.
- Compensation: 2.5% across-the-board increase for non-union staff, 1.0% for union staff per the collective bargaining agreement, plus step increases; blended MPSERS retirement rate of 30.2% ($30.20 per $100 of wages).
- Health care hard caps assume 3.7% medical CPI growth: family $20,180.43 rising to a projected $20,927.11; individual plus one $15,474.60 to $16,047.16; single $7,399.47 to $7,673.25.
- Staffing falls 4.00 FTE (Technology Field Services) to 643.00 total; no new positions.
- Michigan Tax Tribunal reserve set at .25% of tax revenue, roughly $575,500; $12.9 million has been refunded over eleven years.

## Other funds

Shared Services & Tuition Programs (270) budgets $18,078,300 revenue against $19,167,500 expenditures. The ONE fiber network fund (271) spends $2,343,900, including $1,000,000 of infrastructure and $904,100 for Literacy Essentials Oakland. Medicaid (273) passes $12,465,100 through, with $11.7 million returned to LEAs. Three debt service funds carry $3,386,900 of principal and interest. Capital Projects Fund 404 spends $16,928,900 on technical campus renovations; Fund 406 spends $1,295,600 at the Administration Building. The Production Print Enterprise Fund ends at negative $1,115,500 net position; the Risk Related Activity Fund ends at $2,559,200.

## Capital plan

The FY23-FY28 capital plan totals $69,694,300 in needs against $36,600,000 of transfers, with $17,928,900 scheduled in 2023-24 — driven by safety and security work and parking-lot repaving at the four technical campuses.

## Identity

Oakland Schools FY24 Proposed Budget - Enterprise-Wide Executive Summary & Budget Assumptions, Original Budget, March 2023, Fiscal Year 2023-24. Page footers read 03.21.23; embedded Annual Budgeting Amendment Reports are as of 3/14/2023. Oakland Schools is one of 56 Michigan intermediate school districts established in 1962, at 2111 Pontiac Lake Road, Waterford, MI 48328-2736 (nondiscrimination contacts: Assistant Superintendent of Human Resources 248.209.2429, Title IX Coordinator 248.209.2590, Executive Director of Legal Affairs 248.209.2062). It reached the Troy School District board packet dated May 16, 2023 under the ISD requirement to submit a proposed budget to each constituent board by May 1; adoption must occur by June 30.

## Enterprise totals

Proposed FY 2023-24 funding is $440.7 million: property taxes $230.2M, other local and investment revenue $38.3M, state sources $21.6M, other financing and indirect revenue $11.7M, estimated grant awards $138.9M. Proposed expenditures are $455.8 million: salary, wage and benefits $81.5M; purchased services, supplies and dues/fees $21.7M; electric and natural gas utilities $1.0M; capital outlay $20.8M; transfers to LEAs and other funds $188.5M; grant-related expenditures $138.9M; debt payments $3.4M. Both are net of eliminated Risk Related Activity Fund amounts.

## Revenue assumptions

Property taxes rise 5.0%, or $10,962,100, from $219,242,500 to $230,204,600: General Education Fund $13,026,600 to $13,677,900; Special Education Fund $165,688,800 to $173,973,200; Career Focused Education Fund $40,527,100 to $42,553,500. Oakland County taxable values are expected to grow more than 6.0%, but 5.0% is used pending actuals. The base is 70% principal residence, 30% non-principal residence. After eight straight years of Headlee rollbacks, none is expected. Forecast growth is 3.7% (2024-25), 3.0% (2025-26) and 2.5% (2026-27 through 2028-29).

Investment revenue is cut about 40%, from $4,911,800 to $2,886,800: GEF $775,000 to $465,000; SEF $2,340,000 to $1,404,000; CFEF $580,000 to $348,000; Fund 270 $47,000 to $28,200; ONE Fund 271 $290,000 to $174,000; Medicaid Fund 273 $169,000 to $101,400; HR/Finance 277 $16,000 to $9,600; debt service $188,500 to $54,800; capital projects $498,300 to $297,000; Production Print $8,000 to $4,800. Other local revenue falls 2.7%, $36,379,700 to $35,386,700 (Community Telecommunications Network up $467,200 to $600,000; Career Connections rent of $120,000 and a one-time $100,000 Oakland County meal reimbursement both ending). State revenue is nearly flat, $21,559,100 to $21,649,100: Section 81 ISD Operations +2.5% (Governor's budget had 5%), Section 51a +8% (Governor's had 16%), Section 147c MPSERS UAAL Rate Stabilization up as a pass-through, Section 61a.1 CTE down 28% to $1,750,000. Indirect revenue falls to $1,159,500; other financing sources fall 45.0% to $10,545,500. Grant awards are estimated at $138,889,500 (state $68,573,600, federal $69,860,100, local $455,800), down 2.7%.

## Personnel and benefits

No new positions; a 4.0 FTE cut in Technology Field Services follows changes in intergovernmental agreements. Total FTE moves 660.31 (2021-22) to 647.00 (2022-23) to 643.00 (2023-24), with Shared & Field Services / MiPEER dropping 121.00 to 117.00; Business and Operations totals 71.16 FTE and Programs and Services 427.53 (Technical Campuses 177.45, Special Populations 83.00). Non-union staff get 2.5% across the board, union staff 1.0% per contract, plus steps (non-union step growth 1.63%; 1.68% in the SEF forecast). Salaries and wages with FICA rise 8.9% to $51,487,400; MPSERS costs rise 8.8% to $21,530,300. Eight retirement rates apply; the common Basic/MIP with Health Care Premium Subsidy is 28.23% through September 30, 2023 and a projected 31.34% from October 1, 2023, with UAAL stabilization moving 16.65% to 16.89%. The budgeted blended rate is 30.2%, or $30.20 per $100 of wages. Healthcare insurance rises 6.1% to $6,445,500 and other insurances 5.4% to $1,991,700, with employees paying about 13% on average. Hard caps for plan years after 1/1/23: family $20,180.43, individual plus one $15,474.60, single $7,399.47; projected after 1/1/24 at $20,927.11, $16,047.16 and $7,673.25 on 3.7% medical CPI growth. FICA is 7.65%, with the 6.2% Social Security portion applied to wages up to $160,200 for 2023. Workers' compensation runs through the SET-SEG Self-Insurers Workers' Compensation Fund pool.

## Other expenditure assumptions

Utilities rise 12.3% to $1,018,600 (electricity and natural gas bought on the open market from Constellation Energy Services). Purchased services, supplies, materials and dues and fees excluding utilities rise 7.6% to $21,722,500, with GEF up nearly 23% to $6,181,700 for countywide wellbeing initiatives. Capital outlay jumps 288.0%, $5,365,600 to $20,820,200, as capital project funds move $3,840,700 to $18,214,500 for campus safety and security and the ONE Fund adds $1,010,000 of fiber infrastructure. Other financing uses fall 2.3% to $188,484,000. Debt service totals $3,386,900 ($1,460,000 principal, $1,926,900 interest). The Michigan Tax Tribunal reserve is .25% of tax revenue, about $575,500; $12.9 million has been repaid over eleven years.

## General Education Fund (100)

Revenue of $24,344,200 (local $17,063,400, state $6,589,600, other financing $691,200) against expenditures of $24,540,300 yields a planned $(196,100) deficit, an intentional spend-down for collaborative programs and capital projects. Spending splits into General Administration $2,051,700, Finance and Operations $9,420,800, Instructional Services $11,110,000 and Plant & Fixed Charges $1,957,800; FY 2022 actuals were $21,899,613 revenue and $21,537,370 expenditures. Ending equity is $6,557,800 (prepaids $30,800, assigned $2,200,000, unassigned $4,327,000). Section 81 goes $4,269,400 to $4,376,100. School Culture and Climate jumps $952,200 to $2,681,800 (+181.64%); Application Services reaches $2,201,500 and Technology Licensing $1,949,400; LEA and other transfers drop $6,238,400 to $638,400 after a $5.2 million FY23 safety and security transfer. FY23 included $2,050,000 from the Career Connections building sale. Grant Fund 105 budgets $67,654,100 both ways (state $62,848,400, federal $4,628,900), including $25,434,400 to other public schools and $27,333,300 to not-for-profits. The forecast projects unassigned balance of $5.2M (19.9%) in 2024-25, $5.1M (19.9%), $4.6M (17.7%), $4.9M (19.0%) and $4.9M (18.5%) through 2028-29, with capital outlay of $1,238,000 a year through 2026-27 then $238,000.

## Special Education Fund (200)

Revenue of $183,221,900 (property taxes $173,973,200, or 95%; state $7,494,700; indirect $250,000) against expenditures of $183,137,500 yields an $84,400 surplus. Spending: program supervision and direction $2,528,800; program operations $11,017,200; plant and fixed charges $7,824,700; PA-18 base distribution $159,316,800; LEA transfers and program subsidies $2,450,000; School for Deaf/Blind $133,500. The PA-18 base rises $11.0 million, or 7.43%, from $148,300,000; the $2,450,000 covers group home and medical student support, incarcerated youth, startup assistance, extraordinary contingency, assistive technology and Section 24 payments to districts running juvenile detention programs. FY 2022-23 also carried an $8,737,600 additional distribution, $3.7 million of which went out in December 2022; none is budgeted for FY24 pending the FY23 audit. State detail: Section 51a $3,735,400, ISD Membership 51a.2 $62,200, MSB/D deduct 51a.1 $(321,200), State Payment in Lieu of Taxes $1,779,600, Section 147c $1,948,300. Ending equity is $11,524,700: non-spendable $36,500, restricted-special education $1,068,600 and $10,419,600 restricted for future center facility renovations. Policy sets a 5%-10% restricted target; the Board budgets 5%. Special Populations serves about 23,116 students with IEPs through Compliance Support, Capacity Building, Student Services for Low Incidence, the Materials Center/Braille & Large Print Library and Specialized Student Support. Grant Fund 205 budgets $69,201,900 (state $5,678,200, federal $63,523,700), including $56,433,100 to other public schools. Forecast LEA base distributions: $164,915,600, $169,844,300, $173,960,800, $178,178,100 and $182,495,700 through 2028-29.

## Career Focused Education Fund (600)

Revenue of $49,234,000 (property taxes $42,553,500, or 86%; state $5,853,400; other financing $128,100) against expenditures of $49,381,200 yields a $(147,200) deficit. Spending: campus and other program operations $26,828,500; LEA transfers and program subsidies $5,439,500; plant and fixed charges $17,113,200. Ending equity is $6,952,400 (restricted $6,912,400). Section 61a.1 falls 28.23% to $1,750,000; Section 147c rises to $3,150,000; State Payment in Lieu of Taxes is $435,300. Nineteen state CTE program codes run from 501 Agriculture to 597 Computer Systems Networking & Telecommunications across four technical campuses serving roughly 2,700 students from all 28 districts. Campus totals: Northwest $5,395,900, Southeast $5,608,700, Northeast $6,101,600, Southwest $5,780,500 - total campus operations $22,886,700. Four School Resource Officers from the Oakland County Sheriff's Department are added, one grant-funded by the Michigan State Police at the Southwest campus and three locally funded, lifting security lines (Northeast $101,100 to $257,300; Southeast $65,800 to $233,400; Northwest $50,000 to $205,400). Facility lines rise on an anticipated 20% natural gas increase for half the year. Transfers out include $4,400,000 to Capital Projects Fund 404, $3,300,000 to debt service and $104,000 to Fund 406. Regional programs hold at $3.6 million a year, including $3,088,000 of K-12 Career Readiness LEA support, $392,000 early college/dual enrollment tuition and $118,500 for certifications and competitions, plus $1,800,000 of transportation reimbursement and $541,000 (later $543,700) for STEMi. Grant Fund 605 budgets $2,033,500. Restricted balance is forecast at $5.6M (10.7%) in 2024-25 rising to $9.2M (16.5%) by 2028-29.

## Other funds

Shared Services & Tuition Programs Fund 270: revenue $18,078,300, expenditures $19,167,500, ending committed $3,183,600 ($3,265,200 total); shared services revenue $11,169,800; tuition programs are VLAC K-8 (500 FTE, $6,450 resident / $6,650 non-resident), VLAC 9-12 (100 FTE, $6,700 / $6,900), Accelerated College Experience (160 students, $4,900), Graduation Alliance and a KCK, Inc. foreign exchange program for about 50 students. Oakland Network for Education Fund 271, a fiber network with 29 consortium members: revenue $1,252,000, expenditures $2,343,900 (infrastructure $1,000,000, Literacy Essentials Oakland $904,100), ending committed $12,062,600. Medicaid Fund 273: $12,465,100 in and out, distributing $10,725,100 of Medicaid fees, $541,500 of outreach fees and $469,600 of Caring 4 Students payments, retaining no committed balance. HR/Finance Consortium Fund 277: revenue $1,271,900, expenditures $1,293,000, ending committed $366,100; a net $4,875,000 came from the CPDI Fund between FY 2012-13 and FY 2015-16 and the ONE Fund's $.7 million startup grant is fully repaid in 2023-24. School Activities Fund 290: $180,000 in and out, balance $263,000. Debt Service Fund 311 (2016 Refunding Bonds partially refunding the 2007 CFE Campus Renovation Bonds, schedule through 2036) pays $1,460,000 principal and $1,001,900 interest, ending restricted $7,310,800. Fund 313 (2010 Qualified School Construction Bond) transfers $770,000 to Fund 314 and ends at $464,400. Fund 314, the QSCB Construction Reserve maturing 2027, takes a $754,700 federal interest subsidy, pays $925,000 term bond interest and ends restricted $11,341,200. Capital Projects Fund 404 (CFE Technical Campus Renovations Phase II) budgets $4,535,000 revenue and $16,928,900 expenditures - building alterations $8,938,400, improvements other than buildings $6,478,100, technology FF&E $654,400, facilities FF&E $548,000, STEMi $200,000 - ending committed $7,582,500. Fund 406 (Administration Building Renovations, allocated 50% GEF / 24% SEF / 26% CFEF): revenue $562,000, expenditures $1,295,600, ending $10,584,900. Production Print Enterprise Fund 710: operating revenue $1,808,300, expenses $1,990,700, ending net position negative $1,115,500. Risk Related Activity Fund 810: revenue $9,514,300, expenses $9,455,000, $59,300 operating profit, ending net position $2,559,200, with claim fluctuation reserves of $1,000,000 cyber liability, $720,000 professional liability, $276,800 dental and $100,000 health care; compensated absence accruals total $3,427,100 and are fully funded.

## Policy, allocation and capital plan

Policies 3050 (preparation), 3100 (annual budget and amendments), 3150 (fund balance) and 3170 (transfer authority) govern the process, with at least three amendments a year. Targets are 7.5%-12.5% of operating expenditures for GEF unassigned and CFEF restricted, and 5%-10% for SEF restricted net of transfers to districts. Governing statutes are the General Property Tax Act (PA 206 of 1893, MCL 211.24e), the Uniform Budgeting and Accounting Act (PA 2 of 1968) and the Revised School Code (PA 451 of 1976, MCL 380.624 and 380.684), with accounting per Bulletin 1022. Costs allocate 50% GEF / 25% SEF / 25% CFEF generally; 70/15/15 for technology licensing net of revenue; 24/24/52 FTE-based for Financial Services, Enterprise Technical Services, Procurement & Contracting and Human Resources; 50/24/26 by space utilization; 73/25/2 by transportation miles; and 6/75.5/18.5 for property tax administration. Allocated departments total $26,824,200 (GEF $11,730,700, SEF $6,648,600, CFEF $8,444,900), 10.43% of the three funds. Subsidies reported under Policy 3230 total $1,308,800: Illuminate DnA $392,500, Xello $342,000, Nepris $230,000, Discovery Education Streaming $170,000, Atlas Rubicon $144,400, CDX Automotive $15,000, STAMP $14,900. Up to $5 million goes to Literacy Essentials Oakland (LEO 2.0), a five-year project launched in 2019-20; the 22-district MiPEER HR/Finance consortium runs PowerSchool BusinessPlus (formerly SunGard Public Sector, acquired 2017). Mental health work adds two consultants under Section 31n, PREPaRE training with the National Association of School Psychologists and five certified trainers, and support to Oxford plus Ferndale, Oak Park, Huron Valley, Pontiac and Royal Oak. Medicaid billing generates about $11.7 million for LEAs; 91 county schools participate in Michigan Green Schools; COR Advantage purchasing saved 53% per license, over $69,520 countywide in 2022-2023. Oakland County unemployment was 2.5% in December 2022, down from 19.7% in the second quarter of 2020 when nearly 150,000 jobs were lost; 94% of jobs are private sector, and Oakland80 targets 80% of adults with a post-secondary credential by 2030. The 5-Year Capital Plan totals $69,694,300 of needs for FY23-FY28 against $36,600,000 of transfers - $5,499,500 (2022-23), $17,928,900 (2023-24), $16,298,700 (2024-25), $6,976,300 (2025-26), $10,464,800 (2026-27), $12,526,100 (2027-28) - leaving Fund 404 $(6,141,500) short, Fund 406 with $9,053,200 and PP&G $(587,600) at 6/30/2028.
